claim: Mammalian macrophage phenotypes have been intensively studied in vitro.
source: While the mammalian macrophage phenotypes have been intensively studied in vitro, the dynamic of their phenotypic polarization has never been investigated in live vertebrates.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract without specific data or citations in this sentence.

claim: The dynamic of macrophage phenotypic polarization has never been investigated in live vertebrates.
source: While the mammalian macrophage phenotypes have been intensively studied in vitro, the dynamic of their phenotypic polarization has never been investigated in live vertebrates.
evidence: This is presented as a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: A transgenic zebrafish line Tg(mpeg1:mCherryF/tnfa:eGFP-F) was generated in which macrophages expressing tnfa also express fluorescent proteins.
source: We generated a transgenic line whose macrophages expressing tumour necrosis factor alpha (tnfa), a key feature of classically activated (M1) macrophages, express fluorescent proteins Tg(mpeg1:mCherryF/tnfa:eGFP-F).
evidence: The generation of the transgenic line is described in the abstract and detailed in methods.

claim: TNFa is a key feature of classically activated (M1) macrophages.
source: We generated a transgenic line whose macrophages expressing tumour necrosis factor alpha (tnfa), a key feature of classically activated (M1) macrophages, express fluorescent proteins Tg(mpeg1:mCherryF/tnfa:eGFP-F).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about M1 macrophages.

claim: Both aseptic wounding and Escherichia coli inoculation triggered macrophage recruitment.
source: Using 4D-confocal microscopy, we showed that both aseptic wounding and Escherichia coli inoculation triggered macrophage recruitment, some of which started to express tnfa.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy observations described in the results.

claim: Some recruited macrophages started to express tnfa following wounding and E. coli inoculation.
source: Using 4D-confocal microscopy, we showed that both aseptic wounding and Escherichia coli inoculation triggered macrophage recruitment, some of which started to express tnfa.
evidence: This is demonstrated through 4D-confocal microscopy observations.

claim: FACS-sorted tnfa+ macrophages expressed M1 mammalian markers.
source: RT-qPCR on Fluorescence Activated Cell Sorting (FACS)-sorted tnfa+ and tnfa− macrophages showed that they, respectively, expressed M1 and alternatively activated (M2) mammalian markers.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data on sorted cells.

claim: FACS-sorted tnfa− macrophages expressed M2 mammalian markers.
source: RT-qPCR on Fluorescence Activated Cell Sorting (FACS)-sorted tnfa+ and tnfa− macrophages showed that they, respectively, expressed M1 and alternatively activated (M2) mammalian markers.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data on sorted cells.

claim: Pro-inflammatory macrophages converted into M2-like phenotype during the resolution step of inflammation.
source: Fate tracing of tnfa+ macrophages during the time-course of inflammation demonstrated that pro-inflammatory macrophages converted into M2-like phenotype during the resolution step.
evidence: This is demonstrated through fate tracing experiments using time-lapse imaging.

claim: Zebrafish macrophage subsets exhibit diversity and plasticity.
source: Our results reveal the diversity and plasticity of zebrafish macrophage subsets and underline the similarities with mammalian macrophages proposing a new system to study macrophage functional dynamic.
evidence: This is concluded from the experimental observations of different macrophage phenotypes and their conversion.

claim: Zebrafish macrophage subsets show similarities with mammalian macrophages.
source: Our results reveal the diversity and plasticity of zebrafish macrophage subsets and underline the similarities with mammalian macrophages proposing a new system to study macrophage functional dynamic.
evidence: This is inferred from the molecular marker analysis showing conservation of M1/M2 markers.

claim: Macrophages are important immune effector cells with critical homeostatic roles.
source: Currently, it is well established that macrophages are not just important immune effector cells but also cells with critical homeostatic roles, exerting a myriad of functions in development, homeostasis, and tissue repair and playing a pivotal role in disease progression (Wynn et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wynn et al., 2013.

claim: Macrophages exert functions in development, homeostasis, and tissue repair.
source: Currently, it is well established that macrophages are not just important immune effector cells but also cells with critical homeostatic roles, exerting a myriad of functions in development, homeostasis, and tissue repair and playing a pivotal role in disease progression (Wynn et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wynn et al., 2013.

claim: Macrophages play a pivotal role in disease progression.
source: Currently, it is well established that macrophages are not just important immune effector cells but also cells with critical homeostatic roles, exerting a myriad of functions in development, homeostasis, and tissue repair and playing a pivotal role in disease progression (Wynn et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wynn et al., 2013.

claim: Macrophage plasticity and versatility allow them to respond to environmental challenges by modifying their phenotype.
source: The wide variety of macrophage functions might be explained by the outstanding plasticity and versatility of macrophages that efficiently respond to environmental challenges and changes in tissue physiology by modifying their phenotype (Mosser and Edwards, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mosser and Edwards, 2008.

claim: Studies on macrophage subtypes have been mostly performed in vitro using monocyte-derived macrophages.
source: Indeed, although these cell populations have been extensively investigated in mouse and human, these studies were mostly performed in vitro using monocyte-derived macrophages induced under specific stimuli.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of previous research approaches.

claim: M1 macrophages are pro-inflammatory cells associated with the first phases of inflammation.
source: In this classification, M1 macrophages, also referred as classically activated macrophages, are pro-inflammatory cells associated with the first phases of inflammation, while M2 macrophages, also known as alternatively activated macrophages, are involved in the resolution of inflammation and tissue remodelling (Gordon, 2003; Biswas and Mantovani, 2010; Sica and Mantovani, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gordon, 2003; Biswas and Mantovani, 2010; Sica and Mantovani, 2012.

claim: M2 macrophages are involved in the resolution of inflammation and tissue remodelling.
source: In this classification, M1 macrophages, also referred as classically activated macrophages, are pro-inflammatory cells associated with the first phases of inflammation, while M2 macrophages, also known as alternatively activated macrophages, are involved in the resolution of inflammation and tissue remodelling (Gordon, 2003; Biswas and Mantovani, 2010; Sica and Mantovani, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gordon, 2003; Biswas and Mantovani, 2010; Sica and Mantovani, 2012.

claim: Differential cytokine and chemokine production and receptor expression define the polarization state of macrophages.
source: Differential cytokine and chemokine production and receptor expression define the polarization state of macrophages.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about macrophage classification.

claim: Binary M1/M2 naming does not fully reflect the diversity of macrophage phenotypes in complex in vivo environments.
source: However, it is worthwhile to note that such binary naming does not fully reflect the diversity of macrophage phenotypes in complex in vivo environments in which several cytokines and growth factors are released and adjust the final differentiated state (Chazaud, 2013; Thomas and Mattila, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chazaud, 2013; Thomas and Mattila, 2014.

claim: Macrophage plasticity results in a full spectrum of macrophage subsets with a myriad of functions.
source: Therefore, macrophage plasticity results in a full spectrum of macrophage subsets with a myriad of functions (Mosser and Edwards, 2008; Xue et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mosser and Edwards, 2008; Xue et al., 2014.

claim: The possible phenotype conversion of macrophages from M1 to M2 has been suggested in in vitro studies.
source: Although the possible phenotype conversion of macrophages from M1 to M2 has been suggested in in vitro studies, a recent study argues for the sequential homing of M1 and M2 macrophages to the site of injury (Stout et al., 2005; Sica and Mantovani, 2012; Shechter et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Stout et al., 2005; Sica and Mantovani, 2012.

claim: A recent study argues for the sequential homing of M1 and M2 macrophages to the site of injury.
source: Although the possible phenotype conversion of macrophages from M1 to M2 has been suggested in in vitro studies, a recent study argues for the sequential homing of M1 and M2 macrophages to the site of injury (Stout et al., 2005; Sica and Mantovani, 2012; Shechter et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Shechter et al., 2013.

claim: Zebrafish larvae model offers easy genetic manipulation, transparency, and availability of fluorescent reporter lines to track macrophages.
source: We used the zebrafish larvae model for its easy genetic manipulation, transparency, and availability of fluorescent reporter lines to track macrophages (Ellett et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as rationale for using zebrafish, with citation to Ellett et al., 2011.

claim: The existence of macrophage subtypes in zebrafish embryos has been suggested but not fully characterized.
source: While the existence of macrophage subtypes in zebrafish embryos has been suggested, they have not been fully characterized (Herbomel et al., 1999; Ellett et al., 2011; Cambier et al., 2013; Petrie et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Herbomel et al., 1999; Ellett et al., 2011; Cambier et al., 2013; Petrie et al., 2014.

claim: TNFa is a central inflammatory cytokine and well-established marker of M1 macrophages.
source: Here, we report a new reporter transgene for TNFa, a central inflammatory cytokine and well-established marker of M1 macrophages, instrumental to discriminate macrophage subsets during intravital imaging.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about TNFa.

claim: Fin wounding-induced inflammation in zebrafish larvae of 3 dpf triggers macrophage recruitment.
source: Fin wounding-induced inflammation and Escherichia coli inoculation in zebrafish larvae of 3 dpf are two well-established models triggering macrophage recruitment.
evidence: This is stated as an established model system.

claim: E. coli inoculation in zebrafish larvae of 3 dpf triggers macrophage recruitment.
source: Fin wounding-induced inflammation and Escherichia coli inoculation in zebrafish larvae of 3 dpf are two well-established models triggering macrophage recruitment.
evidence: This is stated as an established model system.

claim: tnfa expression was induced in cells accumulated in the caudal fin following amputation (29/33 larvae).
source: Using in situ hybridization, we observed that the expression of the tumour necrosis factor alpha (tnfa), a consensus marker of M1 macrophages, was induced in cells accumulated in the caudal fin and the muscle following amputation (nlarvae = 29/33) and E. coli inoculation (nlarvae = 12/12), respectively (Figure 1A–E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1A-E.

claim: tnfa expression was induced in cells accumulated in the muscle following E. coli inoculation (12/12 larvae).
source: Using in situ hybridization, we observed that the expression of the tumour necrosis factor alpha (tnfa), a consensus marker of M1 macrophages, was induced in cells accumulated in the caudal fin and the muscle following amputation (nlarvae = 29/33) and E. coli inoculation (nlarvae = 12/12), respectively (Figure 1A–E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1A-E.

claim: eGFP-F was undetectable in intact fins of Tg(tnfa:eGFP-F) larvae (10/10 larvae).
source: While eGFP-F was undetectable in intact fins of Tg(tnfa:eGFP-F) larvae (nlarvae = 10/10), it was expressed in cells recruited to the wound at 6 hr post-amputation (hpA) (nlarvae = 16/16, Figure 1F,G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescent microscopy shown in Figure 1F.

claim: eGFP-F was expressed in cells recruited to the wound at 6 hr post-amputation (16/16 larvae).
source: While eGFP-F was undetectable in intact fins of Tg(tnfa:eGFP-F) larvae (nlarvae = 10/10), it was expressed in cells recruited to the wound at 6 hr post-amputation (hpA) (nlarvae = 16/16, Figure 1F,G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescent microscopy shown in Figure 1F,G.

claim: eGFP-F expression was upregulated in cells accumulated in the muscle at 16 hr post-inoculation of DsRed-expressing E. coli (8/8 larvae).
source: Similarly, eGFP-F expression was upregulated in cells accumulated in the muscle of Tg(tnfa:eGFP-F) larvae at 16 hr post-inoculation (hpi) of DsRed-expressing E. coli (nlarvae = 8/8), compared to Phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) injection (nlarvae = 3/3, Figure 1H,I).
evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescent microscopy shown in Figure 1H,I.

claim: Confocal analysis confirmed the presence of membrane-bound eGFP in cells displaying typical myeloid morphology.
source: Confocal analysis confirmed the presence of a membrane-bound eGFP in cells displaying a typical myeloid morphology (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy shown in Figure 1J.

claim: There is consistent overlap between tnfa and GFP-F signal in the fin at 6 hpA (11/11 larvae).
source: We observed a consistent overlap between tnfa and GFP-F signal in the fin (nlarvae = 11/11), showing the direct correlation of eGFP-F and tnfa transcriptional activation in the fin of the reporter line (Figure 1K).
evidence: This is demonstrated by simultaneous detection of tnfa mRNA and GFP-F protein shown in Figure 1K.

claim: eGFP+ cells from wounded Tg(TNFa:eGFP-F) larvae showed significant increase of tnfa mRNA level compared to eGFP− cells.
source: In addition, we FACS-sorted GFP+ cells from wounded Tg(TNFa:eGFP-F) larvae 6 hpA and performed RT-qPCR to analyze tnfa expression. We observed a significant increase of tnfa mRNA level in eGFP+ cells as compared to eGFP− cells (Figure 1L,M).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR data on FACS-sorted cells shown in Figure 1L,M.

claim: The Tg(TNFa:eGFP-F) reporter line recapitulates transcriptional activation of tnfa.
source: All together these results indicate that the Tg(TNFa:eGFP-F) reporter line recapitulates transcriptional activation of tnfa.
evidence: This is concluded from multiple lines of evidence including in situ hybridization, immunofluorescence, and RT-qPCR.

claim: No eGFP-F was observed in macrophages of intact Tg(tnfa:eGFP-F/mpeg1:mCherryF) larvae.
source: In intact Tg(tnfa:eGFP-F/mpeg1:mCherryF) larvae, no eGFP-F was observed in macrophages (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescent microscopy shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Macrophages were recruited to the wound from 1 hpA in double transgenic Tg(tnfa:eGFP-F/mpeg1:mCherryF) larvae.
source: We imaged double transgenic larvae Tg(tnfa:eGFP-F/mpeg1:mCherryF) using 4D confocal microscopy from 45 min post-amputation and found that macrophages were recruited to the wound from 1 hpA, some starting to express eGFP from 3 hpA (Figure 2B,C and Video 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by 4D confocal microscopy shown in Figure 2B,C and Video 1.

claim: Some recruited macrophages started to express eGFP from 3 hpA.
source: We imaged double transgenic larvae Tg(tnfa:eGFP-F/mpeg1:mCherryF) using 4D confocal microscopy from 45 min post-amputation and found that macrophages were recruited to the wound from 1 hpA, some starting to express eGFP from 3 hpA (Figure 2B,C and Video 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by 4D confocal microscopy shown in Figure 2B,C and Video 1.

claim: From 5 hpA, already activated macrophages expressing tnfa arrived at the wound.
source: From 5 hpA already activated macrophages, that is, expressing tnfa arrived at the wound (Video 1 and Figure 2C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by time-lapse imaging shown in Video 1 and Figure 2C.

claim: Infection with crimson-expressing E. coli in the muscle induced the expression of tnfa in phagocytes few hours following infection.
source: Similarly, infection with a crimson-expressing E. coli in the muscle induced the expression of tnfa in phagocytes few hours following the infection (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Video 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Video 2.

claim: tnfa-expressing phagocytes were mainly macrophages.
source: Imaging of the double transgenic larvae Tg(tnfa:eGFP-F/mpeg1:mCherryF) showed that tnfa-expressing phagocytes were mainly macrophages (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Video 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging of double transgenic larvae shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Video 2.

claim: tnfa+mpeg1+ cells displayed flattened and lobulated morphology.
source: tnfa+mpeg1+ cells displayed flattened and lobulated morphology (Figure 2D), while tnfa−mpeg1+ were elongated and dendritic (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: tnfa−mpeg1+ cells were elongated and dendritic.
source: tnfa+mpeg1+ cells displayed flattened and lobulated morphology (Figure 2D), while tnfa−mpeg1+ were elongated and dendritic (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: tnfa+mpeg1+ cells presented a lower velocity (0.32 μm/min) than tnfa−mpeg1+ macrophages (1.09 μm/min).
source: tnfa+mpeg1+ cells presented a lower velocity (0.32 μm/min) than tnfa−mpeg1+ macrophages (1.09 μm/min, Figure 2F) but a higher cell–cell contact frequency (0.036 VS 0.016 contacts/min) with other macrophages (Figure 2G,I,J and Videos 3, 4).
evidence: This is demonstrated by velocity measurements shown in Figure 2F.

claim: tnfa+mpeg1+ cells had a higher cell–cell contact frequency (0.036 contacts/min) than tnfa−mpeg1+ macrophages (0.016 contacts/min).
source: tnfa+mpeg1+ cells presented a lower velocity (0.32 μm/min) than tnfa−mpeg1+ macrophages (1.09 μm/min, Figure 2F) but a higher cell–cell contact frequency (0.036 VS 0.016 contacts/min) with other macrophages (Figure 2G,I,J and Videos 3, 4).
evidence: This is demonstrated by contact frequency measurements shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Macrophage–macrophage contacts of tnfa+mpeg1+ cells lasted longer (48.6 min/contact) than those of tnfa−mpeg1+ macrophages (15.9 min/contact).
source: Measurements of the duration of macrophage–macrophages contacts showed that these contacts lasted longer (48.6 min/contact) than that of tnfa−mpeg1+ macrophages (15.9 min/contact, Figure 2H–J and Videos 3, 4).
evidence: This is demonstrated by duration measurements shown in Figure 2H-J and Videos 3, 4.

claim: Different morphology and behaviour of macrophage phenotypes suggest the existence of macrophage subsets exhibiting different functions.
source: All together these data highlight different morphology and behaviour of macrophage phenotypes in live zebrafish suggesting the existence of macrophage subsets exhibiting different functions.
evidence: This is inferred from the observed differences in morphology, velocity, and contact behavior.

claim: Only 5.6% ± 0.9 (s.e.m.) dbl+ cells were detected in the mpeg1+ population of intact larvae.
source: While only 5.6% ± 0.9 (s.e.m.) dbl+ cells were detected in the mpeg1+ population of the intact larvae, a steady increase of the dbl+ population from 6 to 20 hpA (up to 27.33 ± 0.2%) was observed.
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: A steady increase of the dbl+ population from 6 to 20 hpA (up to 27.33 ± 0.2%) was observed following amputation.
source: While only 5.6% ± 0.9 (s.e.m.) dbl+ cells were detected in the mpeg1+ population of the intact larvae, a steady increase of the dbl+ population from 6 to 20 hpA (up to 27.33 ± 0.2%) was observed.
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: The percentage of dbl+ cells decreased dramatically at 26 hpA to 8.75 ± 1% following amputation.
source: This percentage decreased dramatically at 26 hpA to 8.75 ± 1%.
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In E. coli inoculation experiments, the frequency of dbl+ cells increased as soon as 3 hpi (55.60 ± 0.6%) and remained stable until 26 hpi.
source: In E. coli inoculation experiments, the frequency of dbl+ cells increased as soon as 3 hpi (55.60 ± 0.6%) and remained stable until 26 hpi.
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Wound-induced macrophage activation is transient compared to infection-induced macrophage activation.
source: These results demonstrate that wound-induced macrophage activation is transient compared to infection-induced macrophage activation.
evidence: This is concluded from the comparison of dbl+ cell kinetics between wounding and infection.

claim: High levels of mpeg1 expression was observed in the mCh+ and dbl+ sorted cells at 6 and 26 hpA.
source: As expected, high levels of mpeg1 expression was observed in the mCh+ and dbl+ sorted cells at 6 and 26 hpA (Figure 3D), and high levels of tnfa expression was detected in double-positive populations at 6 hpA (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR on sorted cells shown in Figure 3D.

claim: High levels of tnfa expression was detected in double-positive populations at 6 hpA.
source: As expected, high levels of mpeg1 expression was observed in the mCh+ and dbl+ sorted cells at 6 and 26 hpA (Figure 3D), and high levels of tnfa expression was detected in double-positive populations at 6 hpA (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR on sorted cells shown in Figure 3E.

claim: At 6 hpA, dbl+ macrophages expressed high levels of tnfb, il1b, and il6 compared to mCh+ macrophages.
source: At 6 hpA, dbl+ macrophages expressed high levels of tnfb, il1b, and il6 compared to mCh+ macrophages (Figure 3F,G) that are well-known markers of M1 macrophages in mammals (Mantovani et al., 2002; Martinez et al., 2006).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR on sorted cells shown in Figure 3F,G.

claim: tnfb, il1b, and il6 are well-known markers of M1 macrophages in mammals.
source: At 6 hpA, dbl+ macrophages expressed high levels of tnfb, il1b, and il6 compared to mCh+ macrophages (Figure 3F,G) that are well-known markers of M1 macrophages in mammals (Mantovani et al., 2002; Martinez et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mantovani et al., 2002; Martinez et al., 2006.

claim: mCh+ macrophages expressed low levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines at both 6 and 26 hpA.
source: By contrast, mCh+ macrophages expressed low levels of these pro-inflammatory cytokines at both 6 and 26 hpA (Figure 3F,G), but expressed high levels of tgfb1, ccr2, and cxcr4b (Figure 3H), that are specifically expressed in mammalian M2 macrophages (Mantovani et al., 2002; Martinez et al., 2006; Hao et al., 2012; Beider et al., 2014; Machado et al., 2014).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR on sorted cells shown in Figure 3F,G.

claim: mCh+ macrophages expressed high levels of tgfb1, ccr2, and cxcr4b.
source: By contrast, mCh+ macrophages expressed low levels of these pro-inflammatory cytokines at both 6 and 26 hpA (Figure 3F,G), but expressed high levels of tgfb1, ccr2, and cxcr4b (Figure 3H), that are specifically expressed in mammalian M2 macrophages (Mantovani et al., 2002; Martinez et al., 2006; Hao et al., 2012; Beider et al., 2014; Machado et al., 2014).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR on sorted cells shown in Figure 3H.

claim: tgfb1, ccr2, and cxcr4b are specifically expressed in mammalian M2 macrophages.
source: By contrast, mCh+ macrophages expressed low levels of these pro-inflammatory cytokines at both 6 and 26 hpA (Figure 3F,G), but expressed high levels of tgfb1, ccr2, and cxcr4b (Figure 3H), that are specifically expressed in mammalian M2 macrophages (Mantovani et al., 2002; Martinez et al., 2006; Hao et al., 2012; Beider et al., 2014; Machado et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mantovani et al., 2002; Martinez et al., 2006; Hao et al., 2012; Beider et al., 2014; Machado et al., 2014.

claim: Neither Arginase 1 (Arg1) nor il10 was detected in zebrafish macrophages.
source: Of note, neither Arginase 1 (Arg1), which is largely used as a M2 marker in mouse but not in human (Chinetti-Gbaguidi and Staels, 2011; Pourcet and Pineda-Torra, 2013), nor il10 (data not shown), a known M2 marker in mammals (Mantovani et al., 2002), was detected in zebrafish macrophages.
evidence: This is stated as a negative finding from the molecular analysis.

claim: Arginase 1 is largely used as a M2 marker in mouse but not in human.
source: Of note, neither Arginase 1 (Arg1), which is largely used as a M2 marker in mouse but not in human (Chinetti-Gbaguidi and Staels, 2011; Pourcet and Pineda-Torra, 2013), nor il10 (data not shown), a known M2 marker in mammals (Mantovani et al., 2002), was detected in zebrafish macrophages.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chinetti-Gbaguidi and Staels, 2011; Pourcet and Pineda-Torra, 2013.

claim: il10 is a known M2 marker in mammals.
source: Of note, neither Arginase 1 (Arg1), which is largely used as a M2 marker in mouse but not in human (Chinetti-Gbaguidi and Staels, 2011; Pourcet and Pineda-Torra, 2013), nor il10 (data not shown), a known M2 marker in mammals (Mantovani et al., 2002), was detected in zebrafish macrophages.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mantovani et al., 2002.

claim: dbl+ pro-inflammatory macrophages changed their phenotype at 26 hpA.
source: Importantly, based on the stability of the eGFP in Tg(tnfa:eGFP-F/mpeg1:mCherryF) larvae allowing us to specifically track the behaviour and fate of pro-inflammatory macrophages, we found that the dbl+ pro-inflammatory macrophages changed their phenotype at 26 hpA.
evidence: This is concluded from fate tracing experiments and molecular analysis.

claim: dbl+ macrophages displayed at 26 hpA a significant decrease of tnfa, il1b, and il6 expression level.
source: Indeed, dbl+ macrophages negative for M2 markers at 6 hpA, displayed at 26 hpA, in parallel to a significant decrease of tnfa, il1b, and il6 expression level, a significant increased expression level of ccr2 and cxcr4b (Figure 3E,H).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR on sorted cells shown in Figure 3E,H.

claim: dbl+ macrophages displayed at 26 hpA a significant increased expression level of ccr2 and cxcr4b.
source: Indeed, dbl+ macrophages negative for M2 markers at 6 hpA, displayed at 26 hpA, in parallel to a significant decrease of tnfa, il1b, and il6 expression level, a significant increased expression level of ccr2 and cxcr4b (Figure 3E,H).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR on sorted cells shown in Figure 3E,H.

claim: Early recruited macrophages were still present at the wound area 20 hr later.
source: Recruited macrophages were photoconverted 6 hpA and imaged at 26 hpA revealing that early recruited macrophages were still present at the wound area 20 hr later (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by photoconversion experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Initially recruited eGFP+ macrophages remain at the injury site and still express the GFP.
source: Then, GFP+ macrophages were specifically tracked using time-lapse imaging of wounded Tg(mpeg1:mCherryF/TNFa:GFP-F) fins from 6 to 26 hpA. We show that initially recruited eGFP+ macrophages remain at the injury site and still express the GFP (Figure 4A–C and Video 5).
evidence: This is demonstrated by time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 4A-C and Video 5.

claim: Among eGFP+ macrophages displaying an amyboid phenotype at the wound edge 6 hpA, 50% change toward a fibroblastic phenotype from 11 hpA when they moved distally.
source: The analysis of macrophage behaviour over time shows that among eGFP+ macrophages displaying an amyboid phenotype at the wound edge 6 hpA, 50% change toward a fibroblastic phenotype from 11 hpA when they moved distally (Video 5).
evidence: This is demonstrated by analysis of time-lapse imaging shown in Video 5.

claim: Pro-inflammatory macrophages underwent a phenotypic conversion toward an intermediate phenotype in which both M1 and M2 markers are expressed.
source: All together these data show that pro-inflammatory macrophages underwent a phenotypic conversion toward an intermediate phenotype in which both M1 and M2 markers are expressed.
evidence: This is concluded from the molecular and imaging data showing marker expression changes over time.

claim: Molecular characterization of macrophages in zebrafish reveals the conservation of macrophage subtypes between zebrafish and human.
source: In addition, this molecular characterization of macrophages in zebrafish reveals the conservation of macrophage subtypes between zebrafish and human.
evidence: This is concluded from the similarity of marker expression patterns between zebrafish and mammalian macrophages.

claim: Unpolarized macrophages are mobilized and recruited to the wound following fin amputation.
source: Unpolarized macrophages (mpeg1+) are mobilized and recruited to the wound following fin amputation.
evidence: This is shown in the diagram in Figure 4D summarizing the findings.

claim: Recruited macrophages are activated and polarized toward a M1-like phenotype few hours following fin amputation.
source: They are activated and polarized toward a M1-like phenotype (pro-inflammatory) few hours following fin amputation.
evidence: This is shown in the diagram in Figure 4D summarizing the findings.

claim: After 24 hpA, macrophages progressively change their phenotype toward intermediate phenotypes and maybe fully polarized M2-like phenotype.
source: After 24 hpA, in response to changes in environmental cues, the same macrophages progressively change their phenotype toward intermediate phenotypes and maybe fully polarized M2-like phenotype (non-inflammatory).
evidence: This is shown in the diagram in Figure 4D summarizing the findings, with some speculation about full M2 polarization.

claim: In response to wounding zebrafish, unpolarized macrophages are recruited to the inflammation site and adopt a M1-like phenotype.
source: We propose that in response to wounding zebrafish, unpolarized macrophages are recruited to the inflammation site and adopt a M1-like phenotype.
evidence: This is proposed as a model based on the experimental findings.

claim: Macrophages progressively convert their functional phenotype from M1-like to M2-like in response to progressive inflammatory microenvironment changes within the tissue.
source: Subsequently, they progressively convert their functional phenotype from M1-like to M2-like in response to progressive inflammatory microenvironment changes within the tissue (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is proposed as a model based on the experimental findings shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The TNFa promoter is a 3.8-kb fragment of the zebrafish tnfa promoter, including part of the first coding exon.
source: The resulting plasmid (pI2promTNFa:eGFP-F) harbours a 3.8-kb fragment of the zebrafish tnfa promoter, including part of the first coding exon.
evidence: This is described in the methods section for transgenic line construction.

claim: The expressed eGFP-F harbours the first 7 amino acids of zebrafish TNFa at its N-terminus (MKLESRA).
source: The expressed eGFP-F harbours the first 7 amino acids of zebrafish TNFa at its N-terminus (MKLESRA).
evidence: This is described in the methods section for transgenic line construction.

claim: All animal experiments were conducted according to European Union guidelines for handling of laboratory animals.
source: All animal experiments described in the present study were conducted at the University of Montpellier according to European Union guidelines for handling of laboratory animals (http://ec.europa.eu/environment/chemicals/lab_animals/home_en.htm) and were approved by the Direction Sanitaire et Vétérinaire de l'Hérault and Comité d'Ethique pour l'Expérimentation Animale under reference CEEA-LR-13007.
